headline: December is now priced as a hike, not a cut — so the median stock printed a record relative high while NVDA lost another 3.9%: the AI unwind has become a real-rate problem.
summary: What changed since yesterday is the sign on the Fed. Wednesday's core PCE came in above forecast with GDP revised up and claims at 189,000 (ICSA, 0th percentile of the year), and the December 9 meeting is now priced for a hike rather than a cut. The digest already shows it: the 3-month bill is 4.36% against effective funds at 3.88% and 99th-percentile positioning (+14bp on the month, acceleration z=0.41), while the 10-year real yield sits at 2.79% with acceleration z=0.69 and 22% above its 200-day. Meanwhile 5y breakevens are 2.13% (z=-1.62) and 10y breakevens 2.12% at the 0th percentile. Hot realized inflation, dead forward inflation: that is not a disinflation story, it is the market pricing the Fed breaking demand. The curve agrees — 3m10y has flattened 27bp in a month to 0.51 (z=-0.96) and 2s10s is 0.24 at the 7th percentile. Risk regime -20 versus -19 yesterday; rates composite -47, inflation composite +58.

The tape itself has bifurcated harder, not healed. With US cash shut for the holiday, the rest of the world gapped higher: Euro Stoxx +2.2%, DAX +2.2%, FTSE +1.9%, CAC +1.8%, TAIEX +2.5%, Hang Seng +1.2%, Bovespa +3.7%, EFA/SPY 1m z=1.10 with acceleration z=1.20. Wednesday's US close was the same split: SPX -0.3% and NDX -0.6% against RUT +0.7%, MDY +1.2%, DJT +1.7%, SPW +0.8%. RSP/SPY rose another 1.1% to a 1m z of 2.88 — the 100th percentile of the year. QQQ/SPY is at the 2nd. The damage stayed concentrated in silicon and its power grid: NVDA -3.9% to 149.30, now -30.9% on the month and 26% below its 200-day; ORCL -5.1% and -46.0% YTD at the 2nd percentile; MU -4.5%, ASML -2.5%, TSM -2.0%, GOOGL -2.1%, AMZN -3.1%. But the pace slowed hard — SMH -1.0% after -7.3%, SOXX -0.5% after -8.3%. The liquidation is decelerating, not reversing: SMH is still -22.0% on the month and 19.5% below its 200-day, MTUM 1m z=-2.93, SPHB/SPLV at the 4th percentile, IWF/IWD at the 5th.

Credit is the same pattern — bad levels, better second derivative. HY OAS 3.72 is +34bp on the month and +102bp in three, IG 0.98 and BBB 1.22 are both pinned at the 100th percentile, CCC 14.05 is +520bp YTD. But the acceleration z-scores have turned sharply negative: CCC -2.19, BBB -0.78, IG -0.71, HY -0.69. LQD +0.5% and IEF +0.5% on the day. VIX fell 4.7% to 26.96 from a 34 print Tuesday; the front end of the vol curve is draining while VIX3M rose 3.2% to 26.29, so the inversion is narrowing from 1.0761 rather than flipping. The FX stress epicenter moved: USDBRL -2.8% today after a vertical month, with EWZ +2.9% and Bovespa +3.7% — yesterday's margin-call currency is unwinding. In its place, Mexico. USDMXN +1.3% to 19.69, 1m z=2.22, the 100th percentile, with new tariff proposals the obvious catalyst and MXX -1.3%. DXY is flat at 103.71 but 93rd percentile, AUDUSD 1m z=-2.09, AUDJPY -4.5% on the month.

Commodities keep refusing to confirm the hot inflation prints, with one exception that matters for the consumer. Copper -17.5% on the month (z=-2.69), DBC z=-2.75 with acceleration -2.24, Brent -3.5% today and -19.8% on the month, gasoline -22.4%. That is the demand destruction the breakevens are discounting, and it is why COPX -20.5%, FCX -25.5% and XME -11.6% keep making lows. The exception is natural gas: +10.9% today to 3.626, +34.4% on the month, acceleration z=1.84, 22% above its 200-day — a heating-season tax landing on UMich sentiment of 48. Precious metals snapped back violently off washed-out levels: silver +4.6%, platinum +3.6%, gold +1.9%, GDXJ +4.1%, GDX +3.5% with GDX/GOLD turning up (acceleration z=0.99) and gold/silver -2.6% from a 95th-percentile 86. The one unambiguous domestic uptrend is housing into a falling 30-year mortgage: ITB +2.9% (+9.4% 1m), XHB +2.4%, DHI +3.1%, HD +2.1%, XHB/SPY z=2.34 with acceleration 1.47, housing starts +9.9%. Own the median stock, own shelter and precious metals beta, and stay short the things a hiking Fed and 2.79% real yields price worst.

good.text: Breadth made a new high for the year: RSP/SPY +1.1% to a 1m z of 2.88, the 100th percentile, with SPW +0.8%, MDY +1.2%, RUT +0.7% and DJT +1.7% against an SPX that fell 0.3%. The median stock is fine; the index is a cap-weighted hostage.

Credit is still wide but the widening is decelerating fast — CCC acceleration z=-2.19, BBB -0.78, IG -0.71, HY -0.69, with LQD +0.5% and BKLN acceleration z=0.59. The second derivative turned before the level did.
Front-end fear drained: VIX -4.7% to 26.96 after a 34 print Tuesday, and the VIX/VIX3M inversion is narrowing from 1.0761 rather than deepening. Hedges are being monetized, not panic-bought.

Housing is the one rate-sensitive group accelerating: ITB +2.9% and +9.4% on the month, XHB +2.4%, DHI +3.1%, HD +2.1%, XHB/SPY 1m z=2.34 with acceleration z=1.47, starts +9.9% and the 30-year mortgage 11bp lower on the month at 7.21%.

The world rallied while the US was shut: Euro Stoxx +2.2%, DAX +2.2%, FTSE +1.9%, CAC +1.8%, TAIEX +2.5%, Hang Seng +1.2%, with EFA/SPY 1m z=1.10 and acceleration z=1.20. Non-US equity is absorbing the AI de-rating without the AI weight.
Yesterday's EM blow-up reversed: USDBRL -2.8%, Bovespa +3.7%, EWZ +2.9%, USDINR -0.4% (1m z=-2.78), and gold miners ripped with GDXJ +4.1%, GDX +3.5%, GDX/GOLD acceleration z=0.99.

bad.text: The Fed is now priced to hike on December 9. The 3-month bill at 4.36% sits 48bp above effective funds of 3.88% and at the 99th percentile, the 10-year real yield is 2.79% with acceleration z=0.69 and 22% above its 200-day — tightening is accelerating, and that is unambiguously bad.

Realized inflation is hot while forward inflation is dead: core CPI turning up (z=0.93, acceleration 0.61), core PCE at the 100th percentile, yet 10y breakevens are 2.12% at the 0th percentile and 5y 2.13% (z=-1.62). The bond market is pricing demand destruction, not a soft landing.

The curve keeps flattening into the hike: 3m10y 0.51 after -27bp in a month (z=-0.96, acceleration -0.30), 2s10s 0.24 at the 7th percentile. Historically the worst configuration for cyclical earnings six months out.

Spread levels are still at the wides even if the pace improved: HY 3.72 (+102bp in three months, 97th percentile), IG 0.98 and BBB 1.22 at the 100th percentile, CCC 14.05. HYG/IEF 1m z=-1.31 and rolling over while HYG itself is only -0.4% on the month — the ETF has not marked the damage.

AI capex adjacency keeps breaking with no bounce: GEV -16.3% on the month, ETN -14.3% (z=-2.04, 4th percentile), VST -14.4%, CEG at the 0th percentile, NLR -14.7%, GRID -8.0%, REMX -15.3%. This is the second-order unwind and it is still in train.

Global demand evidence is deteriorating faster than equities: copper -17.5% in a month (z=-2.69), DBC z=-2.75 with acceleration -2.24, Brent -3.5% today and -19.8% on the month, COPX -20.5%, FCX -25.5% — while natural gas +34.4% taxes a consumer already at 48 on UMich.

trades.name: Median stock over the index
trades.line: Long RSP vs short QQQ: breadth at 100th pctile, Nasdaq at 2nd
trades.expr: Long RSP (equal-weight S&P) against an equal dollar short of QQQ. Size 1:1; roll monthly.
trades.thesis: A Fed that hikes into 4.91% tens compresses the longest-duration cash flows first. Mega-cap AI is the duration. The equal-weight index carries the hiking cycle far better: financials, insurance, staples, health care and homebuilders all show turning-up relative strength while XLK relative is -10.7% on the month and rolling over.
trades.trigger: RSP/SPY +1.1% on the day to a 1m z-score of 2.88, the 100th percentile of the year, while QQQ/SPY sits at the 2nd percentile with a 1m z of -1.94. SPX -0.3% versus SPW +0.8%, MDY +1.2%, RUT +0.7% on the same session.
trades.stop: RSP/SPY rolling back under its 1-month average with QQQ reclaiming its 200-day (QQQ is 7.0% below it); or a single-day semis squeeze of more than 6% in SMH that drags the ratio down with it.
trades.target: Another 6-7% of relative outperformance, taking RSP/SPY back toward the 2024 highs.

trades.name: Fade the long-end flight bid
trades.line: Short TLT into a December hike and 2.79% real yields
trades.expr: Short TLT outright, or buy TLT March 80 puts funded by selling 88 calls. Cover half if 30-year yields reach 5.55%.
trades.thesis: The long end rallied 2.5% on the week purely as an equity hedge, not on a change in the inflation path. Core CPI is turning up (z=0.93, acceleration 0.61), core PCE is at the 100th percentile, growth data is firm with claims at 189,000, and the Fed is priced to hike on December 9. A 30-year at 5.30% that is only 3bp lower on the month has no term premium cushion if the hike is delivered with a hawkish dot path.
trades.trigger: TLT +0.9% today and +2.5% on the week on the equity panic bid, while the 3-month bill went to 4.36% (+14bp on the month, acceleration z=0.41) and the 10-year real yield accelerated to 2.79% (acceleration z=0.69, 22% above its 200-day).
trades.stop: A genuine growth break — initial claims above 220k, or HY OAS through 4.25% with the S&P breaking Wednesday's low — would bull-steepen the curve and run this over. Stop on a 4% rally in TLT.

trades.name: Credit hasn't marked the damage
trades.line: Short HYG vs long IEF: HY +102bp in 3m, HYG only -0.4% in 1m
trades.expr: Short HYG against an equal dollar long of IEF, which isolates spread from duration.
trades.thesis: Cash spreads are at the wides of the year — HY 3.72, IG 0.98 and BBB 1.22 at the 100th percentile, CCC 14.05 and +520bp YTD — while the HY ETF is down only 0.4% on the month. A central bank hiking into 14% CCC spreads is the textbook setup for a second leg of repricing, and the refinancing wall gets repriced at a higher front end (bill 4.36%).
trades.trigger: HY OAS widened another 9bp and CCC another 18bp on Wednesday; HYG/IEF carries a 1m z of -1.31 and is rolling over, with IEF turning up (z=0.74).
trades.stop: HY OAS back inside 3.40 with HYG/IEF reclaiming its 50-day — the deceleration in spread widening (CCC acceleration z=-2.19) is the real risk to this trade. Stop at -3% on the pair.
trades.target: HY OAS to 4.25-4.50, roughly 4% on the pair.

trades.name: Shelter is the only cyclical working
trades.line: Long ITB: +9.4% in a month, XHB/SPY 1m z=2.34, starts +9.9%
trades.expr: Long ITB, add DHI as the single-name kicker. Scale in on any pullback to the 50-day.
trades.thesis: Homebuilders are discounting the end of the housing recession, not the Fed's next 25bp. The 30-year mortgage is 11bp lower on the month at 7.21% with acceleration z=-1.15, starts rebounded 9.9%, and the group has already absorbed the worst affordability in a decade. HD +13.1% on the month confirms the read-through to repair and remodel.
trades.trigger: ITB +2.9% today and +9.4% on the month with trend turning up and acceleration z=0.79; XHB/SPY 1m z=2.34 with acceleration 1.47; DHI +3.1%, HD +2.1% on a day the S&P fell.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage back above 7.50% on a hawkish December dot plot, or ITB losing the 200-day (currently 4.1% below spot). Stop at -8%.

trades.name: Gold/silver ratio mean reversion
trades.line: Long silver vs short gold: ratio 86 at 95th pctile, z=2.11
trades.expr: Long silver futures (or SLV) against a dollar-equal short of gold futures / GLD. Express the beta via GDXJ if you want equity convexity.
trades.thesis: The precious complex has been liquidated as a funding source — silver -22.8% in a month, platinum -16.2%, gold -11.5% — and in that kind of forced de-grossing the high-beta leg always overshoots. Gold/silver at 86 is a 95th-percentile, 1m z=2.11 dislocation. The reversion has started and the miners are leading it, which is the usual sequence.
trades.trigger: Silver +4.6%, platinum +3.6% and gold +1.9% today; gold/silver -2.6% off the high; GDXJ +4.1%, GDX +3.5% and GDX/GOLD +2.9% with acceleration z=0.99 — miners outperforming metal is the signature of a bottom, not a dead cat.
trades.stop: Gold/silver back above 90, or silver losing 39 on renewed dollar strength (DXY above 105). Stop at -7% on the pair.
trades.target: Gold/silver back to 77-78, roughly 10-12% on the pair.

trades.name: Peso is the new stress point
trades.line: Long USDMXN: +6.1% in 1m, z=2.22, 100th pctile, tariffs live
trades.expr: Long USDMXN spot/forward, or buy 1-month 20.25 USDMXN calls. Hedge the equity beta with a small short in EWW if you want it cleaner.
trades.thesis: EM stress did not disappear today, it rotated. Brazil's blow-off reversed hard (USDBRL -2.8%), but the new US tariff proposals land squarely on Mexico, and the peso is the most liquid way the market expresses that. A Fed priced to hike while Banxico is easing widens the carry gap in the dollar's favour.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +1.3% to 19.69, +6.1% on the month with 1m z=2.22 at the 100th percentile of the year, 11.8% above its 200-day and still accelerating (acc z=0.37), while MXX fell 1.3% and EWW is -2.6% on the month.
trades.stop: Tariff proposals softened or carved out for USMCA; USDMXN back below 19.10. Stop at -2.5%.

trades.name: Natural gas is the only commodity bid
trades.line: Long natgas: +34.4% in 1m, acc z=1.84, while DBC z=-2.75
trades.expr: Long front-month Henry Hub futures (or UNG), stop below 3.20. Small size — this is the highest-vol line in the digest.
trades.thesis: Every other commodity is pricing demand destruction; gas is pricing winter and structural LNG/data-centre load. The divergence is extreme and the trend is self-reinforcing into December weather. Note the uncomfortable corollary: this is a tax on a consumer already at 48 on UMich, which is precisely why it also hedges the long-housing and long-breadth book.
trades.trigger: Natural gas +10.9% today to 3.626, +34.4% on the month, 1m z=1.73 with acceleration z=1.84 and 22% above its 200-day — against DBC at 1m z=-2.75 and Brent -19.8% on the month.
trades.stop: A warm December shift: close back below 3.20 kills it. Stop at -12%.
